title: Fourth Word Explaining The Comparison And Its Rational Measure

questions.question: In the story, who does the ruler stand for?
questions.answer: Allah, our Creator and Sustainer.

questions.question: What do the two travelers stand for?
questions.answer: One stands for people who pray carefully, and the other stands for people who do not care about prayer.

questions.question: What do the twenty-four gold coins mean?
questions.answer: They mean the twenty-four hours in one day.

questions.question: What does the king’s land stand for?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What does the station stand for?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What is the long trip a picture of?
questions.answer: It is a picture of a person going through life, then to the grave, resurrection, and the hereafter.

questions.question: Do all people travel that journey in the same way?
questions.answer: No. It changes by their deeds and their fear of Allah.

questions.question: What does the ticket stand for in the comparison?
questions.answer: The five daily prayers.

questions.question: About how much time each day is needed for the five prayers and wudu?
questions.answer: About one hour.

questions.question: Why is it a big loss to skip prayer?
questions.answer: Because a person uses almost all day for this short world and does not use even one hour for the hereafter.

questions.question: What example is given to show this is not wise?
questions.answer: It is like giving a big part of your money to a risky game but not giving a small part for a reward that is almost certain.

questions.question: What good things does prayer bring to the spirit, heart, and mind?
questions.answer: It gives them comfort and peace.

questions.question: Is prayer said to be too hard for the body?
questions.answer: No. It says it is not heavy for the body.

questions.question: What can happen to a praying person’s other daily actions if the intention is right?
questions.answer: They can also become acts of worship.

questions.question: How can prayer help a person’s short life in this world?
questions.answer: It can help turn that life into something lasting for the hereafter.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: People who do not pray, and the speaker’s own self that does not want to pray.

questions.question: In the comparison, who is represented by the good servant?
questions.answer: A devoted person who performs the prayers eagerly.

questions.question: In the comparison, who is represented by the careless servant?
questions.answer: A person who neglects the prayers.

questions.question: What does each day’s twenty-four hours get compared to?
questions.answer: Twenty-four gold pieces.

questions.question: What place in the comparison stands for Paradise?
questions.answer: The royal land.

questions.question: What place in the comparison stands for the grave?
questions.answer: The station.

questions.question: What does the whole journey teach about human life?
questions.answer: It teaches that people are traveling toward the grave and the hereafter.

questions.question: What makes some people cover that journey better or faster than others?
questions.answer: Their actions and how much they fear Allah.

questions.question: What worship act is like the ticket?
questions.answer: The prescribed prayers.

questions.question: How much of the day is needed for the prayers and washing for them?
questions.answer: One hour.

questions.question: Why is using twenty-three hours only for worldly life called unfair to oneself?
questions.answer: Because the world does not last, but the hereafter is much longer and more important.

questions.question: What does the passage teach with the example of the lottery and the treasury?
questions.answer: A wise person should choose what brings the greater and surer gain.

questions.question: Which parts of a person are said to feel ease in prayer?
questions.answer: The spirit, the heart, and the mind.

questions.question: What does the passage say about prayer and the body?
questions.answer: Prayer is not a heavy burden for the body.

questions.question: With a good intention, what can happen to the rest of a praying person’s life?
questions.answer: The rest of life can count like worship and help for the hereafter.

questions.question: In the comparison, who does the ruler mean?
questions.answer: Our Lord, Allah.

questions.question: What kind of people do the two servants show?
questions.answer: People who pray sincerely and people who ignore prayer.

questions.question: Why are there twenty-four coins in the comparison?
questions.answer: They match the twenty-four hours of the day.

questions.question: What future home is pictured by the ruler’s special land?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What part of the journey is pictured by the station?
questions.answer: Going to the grave.

questions.question: What comes after that journey according to the passage?
questions.answer: Resurrection and the hereafter.

questions.question: What affects how people pass through that journey?
questions.answer: Their good or bad deeds and their fear of Allah.

questions.question: What does the ticket mean?
questions.answer: Performing the daily prayers.

questions.question: How much time does the passage say prayer needs each day?
questions.answer: Only a small part of the day, about one hour.

questions.question: Why does the passage call missing prayer a great loss?
questions.answer: Because a person gives time to things that disappear and does not prepare for what lasts forever.

questions.question: What is foolish about the example of the person who spends on a game of chance?
questions.answer: He chooses a weak chance of gain over a much surer and greater reward.

questions.question: What feeling does prayer give inside a person?
questions.answer: Calmness and ease.

questions.question: What does the passage say can happen to ordinary actions with the right intention?
questions.answer: They can become worship too.

questions.question: What does it mean that a person can make life permanent in one respect?
questions.answer: The person can use this short life to earn reward for the everlasting life.

questions.question: In the passage, who is the ruler from the story explained to be?
questions.answer: He is Allah, our Sustainer and Creator.

questions.question: What does the praying traveler represent?
questions.answer: A careful, devoted believer who performs the prayers.

questions.question: What does the non-praying traveler represent?
questions.answer: A heedless person who leaves the prayers.

questions.question: What does the royal domain show?
questions.answer: It shows Paradise.

questions.question: What does the station show?
questions.answer: It shows the grave.

questions.question: What larger road is described by the journey?
questions.answer: The road from life in this world to the hereafter.

questions.question: Why do some people move along that road in a better way?
questions.answer: Because of stronger faith-filled actions and fear of Allah.

questions.question: What religious duty is called the ticket?
questions.answer: The five daily prayers.

questions.question: Why is one hour for prayer a small price to pay?
questions.answer: Because it is only a little time compared with the whole day and brings great reward.

questions.question: What mistake does a person make by caring only about this world’s short life?
questions.answer: The person forgets to prepare for the endless life to come.

questions.question: What choice is more sensible in the example: the risky prize or the sure treasure?
questions.answer: The sure treasure is more sensible.

questions.question: How does prayer help the inside of a person?
questions.answer: It brings comfort to the spirit, heart, and mind.

questions.question: How does the passage describe prayer for the body?
questions.answer: It says it is not hard on the body.

questions.question: At the start, which two listeners are called out?
questions.answer: People who leave prayer and the speaker’s own self.

questions.question: In the comparison, who is the master of everything?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What is the difference between the two servants in what they do?
questions.answer: One performs prayer with care, and the other neglects it.

questions.question: What does one full day get compared to in the story?
questions.answer: A set of twenty-four gold coins.

questions.question: What reward-place is pictured by the ruler’s land?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What serious stopping place is pictured by the station?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What does the passage say people are really traveling toward?
questions.answer: The grave, the rising again, and the hereafter.

questions.question: What two things help decide how that journey goes for a person?
questions.answer: The person’s deeds and fear of Allah.

questions.question: In the comparison, what gives a person passage on that road?
questions.answer: The prescribed prayers, like a ticket.

questions.question: How much time does the passage ask for prayer and ablution each day?
questions.answer: One hour.

questions.question: Why is it unreasonable to refuse that one hour?
questions.answer: Because it is a small amount of time for something with very great benefit.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the numbers in the example about winning?
questions.answer: We should choose what has a much better and more certain outcome.

questions.question: What parts of us are said to rest in prayer?
questions.answer: Our spirit, heart, and mind.

questions.question: What can right intention do to normal daily acts?
questions.answer: It can make them count as worship.

questions.question: What is one way prayer makes temporary life lasting?
questions.answer: It lets a person send the reward of daily life to the hereafter.

questions.question: Who does the ruler in the story point to?
questions.answer: He points to Allah.

questions.question: Who is shown by the servant who does his duty well?
questions.answer: A believer who performs the prayers eagerly.

questions.question: Who is shown by the servant who does not do his duty?
questions.answer: A careless person who neglects prayer.

questions.question: What are the twenty-four pieces a symbol of?
questions.answer: The hours in a day.

questions.question: What does the special land stand for?
questions.answer: Paradise.

questions.question: What does the station stand for on the journey?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What does the whole travel picture teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that life is a trip to the hereafter.

questions.question: Do people all reach the end of that trip in the same condition?
questions.answer: No. Their deeds and fear of Allah make a difference.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the ticket in the story?
questions.answer: It means the daily prayers.

questions.question: How much daily time is said to be enough for prayer and wudu?
questions.answer: One hour.

questions.question: What does the passage say about someone who gives nearly all time to this world but not one hour to the hereafter?
questions.answer: That person is harming himself and acting without wisdom.

questions.question: Why is the picture of the lottery used?
questions.answer: To show that people should not choose a weak chance over a far better and surer reward.

questions.question: What benefit does prayer give to the heart, spirit, and mind?
questions.answer: It gives peace and ease.

questions.question: What does the passage say about prayer being hard on the body?
questions.answer: It says prayer is not difficult for the body.

questions.question: With a good intention, how much of a praying person’s life can become worship?
questions.answer: All of it can, in a way, become worship and benefit the hereafter.
